description: Salut! Suntem o echipă pasionată de inginerie, cercetare și rezolvare de probleme tehnice. Ne place să analizăm date reale de la NASA, să lucrăm în Python și să explorăm concepte legate de fizică, date de la sateliți și radiocomunicații/RF.
summary: We developed the Lunar South Pole Landing Site Navigator, a 3D mission-planning workstation designed to evaluate candidate landing sites across the  Artemis Exploration Zone. Powered by a multi-threaded C++17 Crow REST engine and a Node.js, React 18, and CesiumJS 3D lunar globe, the platform integrates NASA LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models, LROC WAC imagery, and NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides.To solve the challenge of identifying safe, operational landing sites, our engine raymarches local crater rim horizons, calculates 60% First Fresnel Zone knife-edge diffraction across S, X, and Ka bands, models LunaNet orbital relay fallbacks (LCRNS-1 / Moonlight-1), and forecasts 30-day solar and communications windows. These telemetry streams synthesize into a real-time Landing Safety Index (LSI) with an automated GO / NO GO decision indicator.At the lunar South Pole, grazing solar angles and Earth libration create severe shadow and communications blackout hazards. By transforming raw planetary topography and orbital mechanics into immediate, actionable mission telemetry, our workstation helps planners de-risk surface operations and enable sustained human and robotic exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

The Lunar South Pole Landing Site Navigator is a full-stack 3D mission-planning and telemetry workstation built to evaluate landing viability across the 85∘S–90∘S85^\circ\text{S}–90^\circ\text{S}85∘S–90∘S Artemis Exploration Zone (152 km radius). Users can click any coordinate on the 3D lunar South Pole, jump to high-priority candidate sites (Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, Haworth PSR, Connecting Ridge), switch RF communication bands (S-Band 2.2 GHz, X-Band 8.4 GHz, Ka-Band 26.0 GHz), or scrub across mission epochs.

When a site, timestamp, or frequency band changes, the browser dispatches an HTTPS POST /api/v1/analyze request to a multi-threaded C++17 REST backend, which executes four physical simulations:

  1. Topocentric Ephemerides: Queries NASA JPL Horizons to compute exact Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation angles for the selected coordinate and UTC epoch.
  2. LOLA DEM Horizon Raymarching: Samples NASA LRO LOLA south-polar Digital Elevation Models to determine local site altitude, peak obstacle distances, and 360° topographic horizon occlusion angles.
  3. RF Diffraction & Fresnel Clearance: Evaluates Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight against the 60% First Fresnel Zone (R0.6F1R_{0.6F_1}R0.6F1​​) criterion to flag knife-edge terrain diffraction warnings across S, X, and Ka bands.
  4. Orbital Relay Fallback: Models line-of-sight geometry to a two-satellite LunaNet constellation (LCRNS-1 and Moonlight-1) whenever Earth is masked by crater rims or lunar libration.

The browser combines the server's telemetry with a 720-hour (30-day) harmonic libration and solar forecaster, rendering 3D illumination and RF vectors directly on the Moon while updating a real-time Landing Safety Index (LSI) HUD (1.0 to 10.0 scale, composite viability bar, and flashing pure-green GO / pure-red NO GO mission annunciator).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Rapid Trade-Space Exploration: Decoupling heavy terrain raymarching into compiled C++17 (-O3) allows mission planners to interactively test hundreds of coordinates, epochs, and RF bands in real time without desktop GIS installations.
  • De-Risking Artemis & CLPS Operations: At the lunar South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at <1.5∘<1.5^\circ<1.5∘ and Earth oscillates across the skyline due to lunar libration. By pinpointing localized permanently shadowed regions (PSRs), RF blackout windows, and relay handoff opportunities, the tool helps prevent power starvation and loss-of-signal events for human landers, robotic CLPS payloads, and surface rovers.
  • Mission-Resilient Architecture: If network latency exceeds 4 seconds or the server is offline, the frontend seamlessly switches to a built-in TypeScript analytical ephemeris and South Pole terrain model so field analysis never stalls.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: C++17, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, Bash.
  • Frontend Stack: Node.js (LTS), React 18, Vite, CesiumJS (WebGL 3D engine configured on Cesium.Ellipsoid.MOON), served via Nginx Alpine.
  • Backend Stack: Crow multi-threaded C++ HTTP microframework (with crow::CORSHandler), libcurl, CMake, GCC (-O3).
  • NASA & Planetary Data: NASA LRO LOLA South Pole Digital Elevation Models, NASA LROC WAC Global Mosaic imagery tiles, NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris API, and official IAU Planetary Nomenclature.
  • Infrastructure & Hardware: Containerized multi-service Docker deployment (:9091 C++ API, :9095 web client) hosted on a dedicated Ubuntu Linux server protected by UPS battery backup and exposed via Cloudflare Argo Tunnels.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, and AI engineering assistants (Google Gemini, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot) used for full-stack scaffolding, ENU coordinate geometry verification, and technical documentation.

Creativity & Key Engineering Factors Considered

  • True Lunar Geodesy Over Earth Defaults: Standard WebGL globes default to Earth's WGS84 ellipsoid, which distorts polar distances and crater geometry. We re-engineered CesiumJS around Cesium.Ellipsoid.MOON (R=1,737.4 kmR = 1,737.4\text{ km}R=1,737.4 km) and projected IAU crater rims using local East-North-Up (ENU) tangent planes for accurate polar navigation.
  • Safety-First Decision Synthesis (LSI): Rather than forcing operators to manually cross-reference six telemetry tables, we designed an aerospace-inspired LSI corner HUD with a hard safety interlock that forces a NO GO state whenever simultaneous solar shadow (CRITICAL_SHADOW) and communications loss (COMPLETE_BLACKOUT) occur.
  • Physical & Operational Factors Modeled: Our team accounted for draconic (27.21 d27.21\text{ d}27.21 d) and anomalistic (27.55 d27.55\text{ d}27.55 d) lunar libration cycles, frequency-dependent Fresnel zone radii, request debouncing (250 ms) during timeline scrubbing, and strict zero-bloat monochrome instrumentation styling for high-contrast readability.
